sense.text:
“Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, gave he them to understand.” The Lord gave each and every one of us a pair of ears, and the Lord is a mastermind. The ear is one of the most precise sensing systems in the body: it catches invisible vibrations, carries them inward, and turns them into electrical signals the brain can understand.

That is the ear gate. Through the ears, what you hear communicates electrically to the brain, where your spirit and your soul are. The ear gate is also called the womb of belief, and this whole teaching is about that gate and the discipline, or lack of discipline, of it unto wicked indulgence. It follows the class on the eye gate, If Thine Eye Be Evil.

“The entrance of thy words giveth light.” Think about an entrance: at an entrance there is a door, or a gate. God’s words have to go through an entrance, and that entrance is the eye gate and the ear gate.

The light is the spiritual understanding, but it is literal too: when the word of God enters through the ear gate it communicates electrically with your brain. It sends a shock wave. That is what is happening when you hear a precept and say, whoa. “It giveth understanding unto the simple.”

The eye gate is called the window to the soul; the ear gate is called the womb of belief. Even the shape of the ear is like a womb. Everything you listen to plants a seed in the mind, and the more you hear it, the more that seed grows into your thoughts, your beliefs and at last your identity, which decides how you act. What you allow to be planted by what you hear conceives things and births things.

So beliefs are birthed by hearing: “how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard?” In order to believe anything, you have to hear it. “And how shall they hear without a preacher?”

precepts.why:
The parable of the four types of Israelites shows the seed being planted by what is heard. “The seed is the word of God.” So the seed you want planted in your mind by way of the ear is the word of God.

“Those by the way side are they that hear; then cometh the devil, and taketh away the word out of their hearts, lest they should believe and be saved.” You cannot believe and be saved without the word being sown in your heart, and it is Satan’s objective to take it out of there.

And this is our goal when we hear this truth, when we say we believe what we have heard of the black Messiah, Jesus Christ, who died for the nation of Israel, of whom we are: “But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.” The goal of planting any seed is that it grows and brings forth fruit. That is how the Lord set up the system of the ear gate.

sense.text: Hearing the word is spiritual. That we are able to hear this word and process it the way we do shows there is something spiritually different about us. “By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand.”

“For this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing.” The prophet spoke this of our people before captivity: we did not want to hear the word of God when the prophets were sent to us. When the understanding came out, our ears were dull of hearing.

“Lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears.” So the Lord has covered the spiritual eyes and closed the spiritual ears of two thirds of our people.

“But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.” If you are really in this truth, and hearing the word of God is truly bringing forth fruit in you, blessed are your ears. Not everybody has the ears to understand this. It is spiritual.

precepts.why:
“He that is of God heareth God’s words.” You have to be of God, predestinated by God, to hear God’s word spiritually for what is truly said.

“Ye therefore hear them not, because ye are not of God.” That goes back to the people whose ears God shut spiritually, the two thirds of our people.

“My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.” His sheep hear his voice, which means the Lord had to fashion your spiritual ears from the beginning. If you are in this truth, that is not to be taken lightly.

This is the clairaudience, the spiritual ears and spiritual hearing, that Bishop Kani taught of in Milk to Meat.

sense.text: This is where it starts. “Yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers.” In the last days the Lord brings out the true teachers of understanding, and your eyes see them.

“And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it.” Many of us came in off social media, but it is always rooted in the camp’s teaching, the prophets prophesying. For those that are of God, the word grabs their spiritual attention. They hear the word behind them: I was raised in the church, I was praying to Allah, I thought I was going the right way, but no, “This is the way, walk ye in it.”

“Ye shall defile also the covering of thy graven images of silver.” A person receptive to what is coming out, wearing a cross, hears the word of God, it convicts them, and it provokes action. They take the graven images and “cast them away as a menstruous cloth”, and “say unto it, Get thee hence.” They throw the idol away.

Many hear the word and Satan comes immediately and roots the seed out, as in Luke 8. But many of us made it past that stage: we heard that crosses were evil, and the pagan holidays, and we got rid of them.

When you see your teachers, hear the word they preach and take heed to it, “Then shall he give the rain of thy seed”, and “it shall be fat and plenteous.” On the surface, our nation was always a nation of farmers living off the land, so the blessing was an increase of the land. For us today it is spiritual: the Lord starts to bless you spiritually when you hear the word of God and take heed to what you hear.

This is what is taking place when you hear the word of God and apply it. Christ is speaking: “Behold, I stand at the door, and knock.” At the door, the gate. “If any man hear my voice, and open the door”: you have to open the door for those words to make the entrance, for the entrance of his words gives light. You have to let him in.

“I will come in to him”: the spirit of Christ enters into you, “and will sup with him, and he with me.” In Isaiah 30 the blessing for taking heed and casting out the idols was plenty from the land. Our blessing today is this: the spirit of the Lord enters into you and sups with you. You eat good spiritually when you let the Lord through that gate.

Many of us made it through the entry-level stage: we heard the word, believed it, even sewed fringes on all our clothes. But it is something you have to do continually. It is not a one-time dinner with Jesus; you have to sup with him every day.

“Apply thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.” You have to apply your ears to the words of knowledge, to be active and intentional in hearing the instruction of the word of God daily.
“My son, if thou wilt, thou shalt be taught”: if you have a willing spirit, you shall be taught. “And if thou wilt apply thy mind, thou shalt be prudent.”

“If thou love to hear, thou shalt receive understanding: and if thou bow thine ear, thou shalt be wise.” To bow your ear means to submit your ear, to give your undivided attention. Black people have a problem with that, especially today with short attention spans; it is a struggle to focus on the word of God. You have to bow your ear, like Mary, not Martha.

“Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave unto him that is wise.” All of this is in the context of hearing and listening. Bishop Nathanyel, Bishop Yawasap, Bishop Kani, the deacons, our leaders, are the wisest men on this earth, and every little sanctuary has leaders the Lord put the spirit of wisdom in and raised up to feed the flock. Cleave to the wise.

“Be willing to hear every godly discourse.” Whenever there is a scriptural conversation and the scriptures are coming out, you are to be willing to hear every one of them. Imagine scrolling past the bishops, deacons and captains premiering live to go listen to No Jumper.

“And let not the parables of understanding escape thee.” It is one thing to get around the wise and hear the understanding come out, but it can escape you if you do not take notes. Sitting in the circle with no Bible, no notebook, nothing in your phone: the Lord said do not let the parables of understanding escape you.

“And if thou seest a man of understanding, get thee betimes unto him, and let thy foot wear the steps of his door.” That is not saying become that man’s best friend and learn his favourite cologne. You may like him and have things in common, but it is not about the man. It is about the wisdom, the spirit the Lord put inside that man.

precepts.why:
The scripture says cleave to the wise, and here is what that looks like: “They enquire at the mouth of the wise man in the congregation.” You should have been inquiring of the wise men in the congregation by now. You have been in for years and never approached the wise in the body with questions, seeking understanding, seeking learning? What the hell are you doing?

“And they shall ponder his words in their heart.” It is not about the person; the person is a vessel, and the Lord can put his spirit on anybody. But whoever the Lord is using to bring the wisdom out of the scriptures, it should not fall on deaf ears. Ponder it in your heart: how does that apply to me, my household, my daily conduct? It cannot be a lovely song to us.

“The heart of the prudent will understand a parable; and an attentive ear is the desire of a wise man.” No truly wise man gets satisfaction from just talking. When the Lord inspires you to bring out wisdom, you desire that the person receive it all.

Imagine being in the spirit, imparting wisdom, and the one you are teaching is not attentive: what was that precept, where we at, read it again. What the hell is wrong with you? Our attention spans are jacked up, but the spirit of the Lord will cause your ear to be attentive if you love to hear. If you get around wise men and your ear is not attentive, you are not fulfilling the desire of the wise, and he might just kick you out.

This is why you ought to wear out the steps of the door of the wise among you. “Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not. Blessed is the man that heareth me.” The me is wisdom speaking in the first person, the spirit of Christ.

“Watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.” So when you are wearing out the steps of the door of the wise, whose door are you really waiting at? Wisdom’s. With wisdom you always get what you put in; the Lord gives wisdom according to your own desire, and the more you are around the wise for their wisdom, the wiser you become.

That is the law of succession: when they perish from the earth, the spirit still remains in you because you cleaved unto them, and you might even have a double portion.

sense.text: “Bow down thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply thine heart unto my knowledge.”

“For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee”: it is pleasant to keep the words of the wise within you. “They shall withal be fitted in thy lips.” From cleaving to the wise and hearing their words, what you are receiving is what will come out. That knowledge becomes fitted in your lips.

precepts.why:
“The Lord God hath given me the tongue of the learned.” In order to learn, you had to listen, hear and hearken. Now it carries over from your ear: you are no longer only a receiver, you have the tongue of the learned, “that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary.” You can strengthen and comfort your brothers and sisters with the same wisdom you were desiring and listening to.

“He wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as the learned.” You never have learned enough and you never arrive. Watching all the classes and reading the Bible through does not mean you have arrived; he that eats wisdom shall yet be hungry. That is why it says watching daily at my gates: let Christ in and sup with him daily.

When your hearing is exercised over a period of time, you become learned and develop a different level of spiritual ears.

sense.text: “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots.” This is speaking of Christ.

“And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.” This goes into the seven pillars of wisdom that Bishop brought out.

“He shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears.” That does not mean he will be deaf to what anyone has to say. He will not decide by what his ears hear: the Messiah will not be misled by rumour, accusation, partial testimony or popular opinion. That is how we processed what we heard carnally, when we were in the world: rumours, accusations, popular opinions, persuasions. The spirit of Christ is not so.

His knowledge is complete and his verdicts perfectly true. Not reproving after the hearing of his ears is a discerning spirit over what comes through the ear gate. Christ showed this discernment in his earthly ministry, knowing what was in man and answering those who sought to test or deceive him.

precepts.why:
“I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” Read in its totality, Christ is not self-willed; he goes by the will of the Father.

So what does “as I hear, I judge” mean, when Isaiah 11 says he will not reprove after the hearing of his ears? The authority to judge belongs to Christ because the Father entrusted judgment to the Son, and his judgments proceed from the Father’s perfect knowledge, truth and righteousness, not from outward appearance or partiality. Where is the Father’s perfect knowledge found? In the scriptures. Christ processed everything he heard through the filter of his Father’s word, listening to the Father’s assessment before every verdict.

That is how we have to be. We do not respond from our carnal understanding and how we feel; we respond by how the Lord tells us to process what is heard. I may feel this way, but what does the Bible say about what I just heard? That listening is an intimate, continual communion, and that communion is not the bread and crackers of the Christian church. It is studying daily, searching the scriptures daily, letting the spirit of Christ in to sup with you. Our lives must be guided by God’s voice rather than human impulse.

sense.text:
When you let the spirit of Christ in and bow your ear and receive instruction, the Lord fits those words in your lips; you have the tongue of the learned because you have the ear of the learned. With that ear you discern what you hear differently from the average person, because the word of God interprets it.

“For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat.” Taste is a sense. In the Old Testament, to taste is often used figuratively to mean to discern, to perceive or experience a thing directly rather than only hearing about it. So as the mouth tastes meat, the ear tries, discerns, words.

precepts.why:
“The belly devoureth all meats, yet is one meat better than another.” All clean meats, but there are grades and levels of meat: white meat, dark meat, tender, tough, different cuts. Brothers bring out the grills at the Feast of Tabernacles and some are meat connoisseurs.

“As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison”: with the lights off and the room pitch black, you can tell chicken from steak by the taste. “So doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” You know what the word of truth sounds like, what goodness and honesty sound like, because you study this word and hear it regularly. So when something is off, your spiritual ears taste it at once: something is not right about that. That is the spirit of discernment.

sense.text:
All of that is the building block of becoming spiritual in your hearing and developing clairaudience: you come into the truth, bow your ear, cleave to the wise, the words are fitted in your lips, you have the ear of the learned and can detect false speeches. That is good and gravy, but it is never permanent.

“My son, attend to my words; incline thine ear unto my sayings.” Incline your ear to God’s sayings.
“Let them not depart from thine eyes; keep them in the midst of thine heart. For they are life unto those that find them, and health to all their flesh.”

“Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.” Keeping the heart is not being an organ donor. When the words, the understanding and the spirit are in the midst of you, you have to keep them, protect them, guard them. To keep your heart with all diligence means to guard it: guard your spirit, guard your mind, guard the gates.

precepts.why:
The Korahites “were over the work of the service, keepers of the gates of the tabernacle: and their fathers, being over the host of the Lord, were keepers of the entry.” What is each of us? A spirit inside an earthy tabernacle. Proverbs 4 says keep his words in the midst of thee, and to protect what is inside you, you have to keep the gate.

These men guarded the thresholds of the tent of meeting, controlling access and preserving the holiness of the place where the Lord met his people. The work required alertness, obedience and reverence, for no one was to treat God’s dwelling as common, and their inherited service joined the generations of Israel in guarding the worship of the Lord. That is what keeping means.

These are the chapters people rush through and skim, but the Korahites who guarded the door of the tabernacle represent what each one of us has to do spiritually every single day.

“And Berechiah and Elkanah were doorkeepers for the ark.” The ear gate and the door are interchangeable: gate and door are both entrances. These doorkeepers were guardians, and guarding is a duty of active protection. The ark could not be touched or viewed irreverently.

Their post was spiritual as much as physical: guarding the ark meant guarding the covenant testimony of God among his people, and their vigilance reminded Israel that access to God is by his appointed way, not casual, not presumptuous. That is how we have to be with our eye gate and our ear gate: guard it with all diligence and with reverence.

Why guard it? The Lord is speaking to Cain before he did what he did: “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” That is why you have to guard the door: sin lies at the door, waiting on you.

“And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” If you let sin and Satan in the door, it eventually rules over you. Just as you let the spirit enter in and are moved by the spirit to bring forth fruit, if you are not guarding your eye gate and ear gate and let evil enter, that becomes what moves you to say what you say, do what you do and think what you think.

sense.text: “For I delight in the law of God after the inward man.” You might think there is only one law that enters in, God’s law.

“But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind.” There is another law, contrary to the law of God, in your members, in your ear. A law implies instruction and commands. The Bible says don’t hate your brother; then the other law in your ear says, thou shalt cuss him out, thou shalt crash out, this is how we do it. That is the other law of your members, commanding you contrary to the word of God.

“And bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.” That is what happens in war: you take captives. Satan’s objective is to have us captive to his will.

precepts.why:
The Lord likens the congregation to a body: all of us are members playing certain positions, as the parts of your body have different functions. “For the body is not one member, but many.” Then it names the members: the foot, the hand, and “if the ear shall say, Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?”

So one of our members, the one this teaching is about, is the ear. When Paul says another law is in his members, that law is at work in the ear.

Dealing with the ear, be mindful: something there will speak to you and command you to do things contrary to what God said. It is always at the door.

“Cease, my son, to hear the instruction that causeth to err from the words of knowledge.” All of us have instructions that come to us telling us to go against what God says, and the Lord says cease to hear that. Don’t fall for it.

sense.text:
Where do the instructions to go against God come from? Who raised you? “Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world.” A course is instruction: in time past we all walked according to the instruction of this world.

“According to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience.” The prince of the power of the air is Satan, so in time past we all followed Satan’s instructions. The air pictures an unseen realm: Satan’s influence is real though invisible, pervading society like the air we breathe, limited and temporary but deadly to the unaware.

Think of the airwaves, the radio waves and electromagnetic frequencies that carry radio, television and phone and wireless signals: the invisible paths through which audio and video travel. The class itself is streaming right now; you do not see the form of a voice, yet it is heard on the West Coast and overseas. So there is a prince, a power figure, ruling the airwaves, and that is Satan.

precepts.why:
“And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world.” This is not the story of Lucifer the choir director getting mad at God and getting kicked out of heaven. This is prophecy, to come. That old serpent is the same word as in Genesis.

“He was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him”: his angels are his allies. This is future prophecy of the destruction of Edom.

sense.text: It does not say Edom or man; it says dragon and serpent. “And behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.” It seems mythological, but watch.

“And the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born.” Revelation 12 gives a historical reference so that the prophecy can be understood. The great red dragon stood before the woman to devour her child as soon as it was born, and Matthew 2 shows who the dragon is.

precepts.why:
“Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt”: take the young child Christ into Africa, where they could blend in with the other dark people. “For Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.” That is what Revelation 12 says of the great red dragon, but it is a person, descended from a people.

Who is Herod? So-called Herod the Great and his family had zero melanin, yet he was the so-called king of Judea, and he was and is the red dragon. Herod was an Idumean, the same as an Amalekite, and Amalek was the bastard grandson of Edom, a notable lineage of Esau in Genesis 36. He is called one of the hereditary enemies of the Jewish people. Of course he would try to devour the child that would be the Messiah as soon as it was born: he is a perpetual hereditary enemy of God’s people. And if you are a hereditary enemy of God’s people, whose people are you?

“Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come”, the day of the Lord’s return, “except there come a falling away first”: we had to fall away into slavery first, starting in 70 AD when Jerusalem fell and we were led captive into all nations.

“And that man of sin be revealed.” Satan, the prince of the power of the air, is the spiritual demon, but there is a man of sin. He has to be revealed because he wears a disguise; he deceives the whole world, showing himself as something he is not but the opposite of. “The son of perdition”: a son is his father’s heir, so he is destined to inherit perdition. This is a people, an actual race.

“Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.” Look at the white Christ they put up as God: look at those feet, that is no fine brass burning, that is crackers, salt crackers, milk of magnesia. He is not in the midst of any seven candlesticks; he is showing himself that he is God. And it is not only the Christians. Herod’s people, his descendants, parade in the temple of God as God’s people, yet are against everything God says, because they are the hereditary enemies of God’s people. They are the vessels of Satan in the earth.

sense.text:
“And the serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood after the woman, that he might cause her to be carried away of the flood.” The serpent is the so-called white man, the Edomite race. The flood is not Katrina and the broken levees. It is the great voice out of his mouth.

That flood is propaganda, to stop the elect from hearing this truth and throw them off with false narratives about us, as our forefathers suffered in the time of Ezra, Nehemiah and Zerubbabel. As he stood before the woman to devour the child as soon as it was born, he casts that flood on all our people, just in case, because the war is against the remnant that fear God and keep the commandments, and he does not know which of us will be part of that remnant. So he casts his great voice, his media, on all of us.

precepts.why: Who is the woman? “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.” The daughter of Zion is the people of Zion, Israel, us. That is who the Bible is speaking of.

What is the water out of the serpent’s mouth? “Because the Lord hath spoiled Babylon, and destroyed out of her the great voice.” When a voice is loud, you hear it, and Babylon has a great voice. “When her waves do roar like great waters, a noise of their voice is uttered”: the great voice is likened to roaring waters. So the white man uses his great voice to carry away the woman with that flood.

Every aspect of the media is called Jewish: the so-called Jews run the television networks, the radio networks, the airwaves. They are the prince of the power of the air, and the Bible backs it up.

“I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich)”: that is the real Jews, rich because the blessings and promises of the Bible pertain to us and not to them. “And I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” They show themselves as God’s people, but they are not.

A synagogue is a place like a temple. We are the temple of God, the vessels in which the spirit of God dwells; the fake Jews are the synagogue, the temple, of Satan: the human vessels, the spawn of the spiritual demon Satan in the earth. He is the one with the great voice flooding our minds with the garbage they put in the media.

And media is the plural of medium, and a medium is one who acts as a bridge between the physical world and the spirit realm, communicating with spirits and higher entities to relay messages to the living. The higher entity they relay for is not the Most High; it is Satan. Everything Satan wants you to think, feel, say and do, he relays through his vessels, which is why they have power over the media: to get in through your eye gate and your ear gate, all the gates.

sense.text:
Satan tells his mediums what to communicate to us. “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” In context Paul was speaking of a false doctrine of the resurrection, saying don’t entertain it, it will corrupt your faith. But as a general principle, evil communication has the power to corrupt the good manners that come from God. And another word for communications is media: evil media corrupts good manners.

Music is an extraordinarily powerful medium of communication. It bypasses literal language, and it bypasses the prefrontal cortex, the part of the brain of logic and reason, to engage the brain, the body and the emotions directly. Unlike speech, it lights up nearly the whole brain at once, memory, emotion and motor systems: that is a lot of places where seeds are being sown in your spirit. It triggers a cocktail of chemicals, dopamine for pleasure, oxytocin for bonding in group singing. Music predates written and spoken language, and babies respond to melody and emotion long before they understand words.
“Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?” The Lord is speaking to Job. He was there, but he does not remember; there is no remembrance of former things.
“Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?” Who stretched the line upon the earth, and “who laid the corner stone thereof”?

“When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?” Before the foundation of the earth was fully laid, the morning stars were singing. There was music in the heavens before the earth was established, and it was righteous music. Music is not powerful only to do evil. Then where did evil music come into play? Genesis 4.

Here is the original white man, the FCA: the foundational Caucasian Antichrist. “And Cain went out from the presence of the Lord, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.” The land of Nod went on to be known as Babylon, the original. That is why Edom is called the daughter of Babylon, as we are called the daughter of Zion: that is where each comes from.

“And he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.” He built a city in the land of Nod and began reproducing. Cain was extremely powerful and ruled the city of Enoch, the original Babylon, yet he went out from the presence of the Lord. So what gave him his power to rule? In occultism Cain is revered as the first witch, the spiritual ancestor of the craft. Cain is the father of witchcraft.

“And his brother’s name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.” From Cain’s lineage came Jubal, the originator of all that handle the harp and organ. Was Jubal dealing with God? No: he was dealing with the witchcraft he learned from his father and his folks.

The word music comes from the Greek for the art of the Muses, the nine Greek goddesses over the arts. The Greeks understood that this art form did not come from the earthly realm. Michael Jackson said the same: that he did not write his songs, that he was a tunnel they came through, that they were already written somewhere in space and some higher force made it happen. His hit songs were downloaded from the spiritual realm.

precepts.why:
We have righteous music too, but that does not change where music comes from. “But none saith, Where is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night.” Think of King David: the Psalms are a compilation of the greatest hits, and David’s songs came from the Most High while he was in the spirit. God gives us our righteous song, and that is why righteous music moves you a certain way.

But did Billie Jean come from the Lord? Hell no. Your ear has to taste that: there is no precept, wisdom or knowledge in it. If it does not come from God, where does it come from? That is the spirit that was operating in Jubal.

sense.text:
Remember Cain’s seed, the foundational Caucasian Antichrist. “For the bewitching of naughtiness doth obscure things that are honest.” Bewitching, and who is the father of witchcraft? Cain.

“And the wandering of concupiscence doth undermine the simple mind.” Concupiscence is lust. That is the other law in your members telling you to go here and there, listen to this, watch this, and it undermines the simple mind.

To undermine is to make someone weaker and less effective, gradually, secretly or indirectly; to erode confidence, authority and trust in a group. That is why the BBC and the SPLC are used: to erode your confidence in where you congregate. In its physical sense, to undermine is to dig beneath a structure, or to wash away the material underneath until it collapses. What do you wash with? Water. And what is the serpent’s voice? A flood of waters. The media is the water.

When water flows continuously against a rock, it slowly erodes the softer layers beneath; as the foundation is hollowed out, the rock loses its support and collapses. That is undermining through bewitching, and that is Satan’s end goal for every one of us. From the beginning they dealt in music through witchcraft, as mediums of Satan; he will surely weaponize it to destroy our minds in Christ.

precepts.why: Who is that rock being undermined? “They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

“For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.” Each one of our foundations is the rock, Christ, that we opened the door to and said, come in and sup with me.

Satan, who also lies at the door, wants to undermine that. He wants to erode your belief in Christ until you evict him, drive him out of you as his dwelling place. Music roots deep, down to the DNA; a song from before the truth comes on years later and it is still in there.

sense.text:
Music has the power to make you sick or to heal you, and here it is in the Bible, what David did for Saul: “when the evil spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.” Music has spiritual healing power.

But Satan, the god of this world, the prince of the power of the air, wants the opposite. There are frequencies that make you sick and destroy you. The music industry was moved off 432 hertz to 440, which keeps people agitated, anxious and easy to control; the frequency under the beat stirs rage, lust and depression, while healing frequencies are buried. This is how you know what captivity we are in: the white man is the devil the Bible speaks of. The lyrics are one thing, but the frequency of the beat alone throws you off.

Music is one of the most powerful catalysts for neuroplasticity, the brain’s rewiring of itself. Being born again in this truth is a rewiring: you heard the word, renamed yourself, started congregating every Saturday, changed your clothes and put on fringes. Music can wrap cords of sin around all of that. It can change your whole spirit.

The beats and the frequencies are one element of the warfare, but there is a willful element too, and it makes no sense to do this willfully. “It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.” A rebuke from the wise hurts sometimes, but it is better than the song of fools. A fool is a soul without knowledge; the world’s artists have not one ounce of God’s wisdom, knowledge and understanding.

The music industry is demonic. Future, who calls himself Pluto, a name of Hades, and the wizard, is a high-level warlock: he speaks to the devil in his songs, pushes drugs, sex, money and covetousness, records in the dark by candlelight, the way witchcraft is done, summoning spirits so the music reaches the hearts of the people. Before the truth, one Percocet at his concert showed it: it doesn’t make you feel good, but you are under a spell.

And there is a genre that pushed murder and turned every city’s murder rate up. One who listens to drill ten hours a day says his thoughts get demonic and it infiltrates his mind. The children in juvenile wake up at six in the morning like that, hacking school computers to hear it. Give them the phones and tablets and you wonder why they talk about a blicky.

Music bypasses the conscious filters and goes straight to the subconscious. Sound reaches the emotions and the body before the rational mind can evaluate it, before you can block it out, and the seed is sown. Rhythm moves your body before you decide, the foot tapping and the head bobbing when a wicked song plays in the store. Melodies are bound to deep memories; a song not heard in twenty years comes back word for word, and a familiar song can resurrect the old man we killed when we came into the truth.

Lyrics work like affirmations, gradually normalizing and reinforcing underlying beliefs. The ear is the womb of belief: listen to wicked music every day and you will start to believe it. You will tell yourself you have opps when you have no problem with anybody, and come to the school needing somebody to be the opp.

This is something that does not even require you to watch it, and it has taken the place of television for many: the podcast. “The discourse of fools is irksome.” Discourse is conversation, and the conversation of fools is supposed to be irksome to your spirit. “And their sport is the wantonness of sin”: that is what they do for fun.

Since COVID, podcast listening has gone up astronomically in Babylon, to hundreds of millions of listeners, and it is projected only to increase. Many brothers and sisters are entertaining worldly podcasts, listening to fools. Some of it is good information; most of it is not: people drinking their own blood, boasting of cheating, saying there was never slavery, calling AI their religion.

You tell yourself it isn’t sin, it isn’t real music, it isn’t a bad podcast, it is just at the gym. But Satan is more subtle than any beast of the field, and anything outside of God he will work some evil in, and you are sowing it into your spirit.

precepts.why: “As is a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool: and the knowledge of the unwise is as talk without sense.” The discourse of fools, talk without sense: that is the podcast, listening to fools and the knowledge of the unwise.

Listening to podcasts, your brain processes the stuff as valid information without putting it through any process of validation. “The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.”

You may say, I don’t believe everything they say, I leave the bones. But Satan knows how to tap into your subconscious mind. The seed is being sown, laying underlying beliefs in your mind that are contrary to God. You have to be very mindful.

“A wholesome tongue is a tree of life: but perverseness therein is a breach in the spirit.” A wholesome tongue that utters sound, comfortable and useful counsel preserves the present life and promotes the spiritual and eternal life of speaker and hearers. A perverse tongue, all sorts of false and corrupt speeches, breaches the spirit.

That is the podcast: false information and corrupt speech. Some went on an Andrew Tate binge: he says some things, but in it is a whole lot of whoremongering, covetousness, evil and rebellion. When you are in the spirit, that stuff is like vomit.

Perverseness disturbs, wounds, and often corrupts and destroys the spirits or souls of both the speaker and the hearers, just as evil communications corrupt good manners. Go back to the proverb: guard your heart. Even gathering content for the radio defiles the algorithm; a few seconds of scrolling and the world and wicked memories come up. Set the phone face down when you read the Bible. This affects you spiritually.

This is how each of us is supposed to be in this truth. The great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, and who was righteous in Sodom? “And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.”

“For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day”: seeing and hearing, the eye gate and the ear gate. Filthy conversation is supposed to make you sick. Like Lot, we should be sensitive to sin and feel spiritual discomfort when unrighteousness hits the ear gate.

Lot’s account warns of becoming too comfortable in a sinful environment. Listening to No Jumper and Drink Champs for two or three hours at the gym or in the car until it doesn’t bother you: that is being too comfortable. Satan is in the door, in the building. Some of it is only information and not harmful, but you have to stay on guard and be a diligent doorkeeper of your eye gate and your ear gate. Single brothers and sisters convinced R&B is not evil: it puts a lustful spirit on you. We have to be vexed with the filthy conversation.

sense.text: Now the ear gate inside the congregation. Many brothers and sisters, especially when new to this truth, want to entertain other doctrines. “Through desire a man, having separated himself, seeketh and intermeddleth with all wisdom.” Through desire, through lust. We read the King James 1611 and bring out precepts on every subject, but that is not enough for some: because a scripture says as it is written in the book of Jasher, they go after books the Lord did not gather with his spirit, some evil, perverse, weirdo stuff. Don’t do it. Entertaining all sorts of doctrine is dangerous.

precepts.why:
“And he gave some, apostles”: he gave us leaders, the bishops and deacons. “And some, prophets”, with the gift of prophecy; “and some, evangelists”, the brothers who hazard their lives travelling across the seas, Deacon Isaac, Captain Joel, Captain Yuri back from Papua New Guinea, Bishop Nathanyel, Bishop Kani, Deacon Malachi from Haiti. That is true evangelism. “And some, pastors and teachers”: those the Lord raised up to feed the flock in the local sanctuaries.

“For the perfecting of the saints.” That is why God put these teachers in place: whatever he put in their spirit to feed the flock with is sufficient to perfect us. “Till we all come in the unity of the faith”: God’s will is that we all be unified in one faith, believing the same thing, and that comes through the teaching he inspired the teachers to teach.

“That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive.” Entertain teachings outside the apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers God gave us, and you will be carried about with every wind of doctrine. The ones on the name doctrine, multiple wives, Sabbath at sunrise, all bugged out: crackheads now, crackhead sodomites. That is their fruit. Leadership was not teaching that, but you went and entertained it.

That is an instrument of Satan. He knows the Lord did not gather every book. One posts that Enoch helped him understand the fallen angels and the Nephilim, goes off the deep end, and a few months later is smoking weed, keeping no Sabbath and no holy day, whoremongering.

Do not think you can survive in this truth only by watching classes. The classes tell you to read; Bishop charges us to read four chapters a day; those who received the word with readiness searched the scriptures to see whether those things were so. Every one of us has to study the Bible on our own time. “Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.”

“But shun profane and vain babblings”: dumb doctrines. Once your senses are exercised and you have the ear of the learned, some may watch certain things to know what we are up against, but most are not built for that. You do not need to be watching apologists and weird doctrines. Build a strong foundation in what is taught here first.

“For they will increase unto more ungodliness”: down a deep, evil rabbit hole. “And their word will eat as doth a canker”: it eats at your spirit, the undermining again. Of them were Hymenaeus and Philetus. Hymenaeus, as First Timothy 1 tells, was a member put out for blaspheming, who started his own thing and pushed another doctrine, “saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some.” He took brothers and sisters out of the truth with that false doctrine.

Some come to the Sabbath in purple and gold, then go congregate with a brother who was put out of the body, saying they are only building him up. Stop playing yourself.

“Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.” “For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly.” They are not trying to build you up unto salvation. They want to seem to have wisdom our leaders do not: follow me, we understand what they don’t. That person does not care about your soul.

“And by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” That is the bewitching of naughtiness that undermines the simple mind, the mind not guarding its eye gate and ear gate. They entertain it, fall for it, and fall out of this truth.

sense.text: Murmurers and complainers: every school has them. “These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts”, doing their own thing, “and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men’s persons in admiration because of advantage.” They turn the truth into a social club: get around so-and-so and you’ll be travelling. With that same tongue they murmur and slander. They are carnal, looking at the truth from a carnal perspective, like the Corinthians saying I am of Paul, I am of Apollos. Mark people like that, that clique spirit; they are not about the unity of the faith.

precepts.why: “Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace.” That does not mean cast a spell on them. When somebody comes to you with a rumour, gossip or backbiting, put the fear of God in them: you have the devil on you, and God will condemn you if you do not get that spirit off you. As Peter told Simon, I perceive thou art in the gall of bitterness; your heart is not right in the sight of God; pray the Lord forgive the thought of your heart. Those who come whispering and murmuring should leave shaking and trembling at the word of God you rebuke them with.

“Well is he that is defended through the venom thereof.” Evil speeches, murmurings, whisperings and backbitings are poison. You could have been at perfect peace with a brother or sister, and leadership had no evil thought, but you entertained what somebody murmured to you. Nothing verified, nothing confirmed, not witnessed, not established by two or three witnesses, but now you look at leadership and your brother differently. That seed has been sown, and you are decaying spiritually as the poison spreads through the body.

“Who hath not drawn the yoke thereof, nor hath been bound in her bands.” The key word is defended. That goes back to keeping your heart with all diligence, guarding the gates and doors of your spirit, your eyes and your ears. Defend yourself from foolishness, because it takes root and destroys the fruits of the spirit.

These things were written aforetime for our admonition. When the Lord’s mission is clear and somebody speaks contrary to sway your belief, do not give heed, because the ear is the womb of belief.

“And ye murmured in your tents, and said, Because the Lord hated us, he hath brought us forth out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us. Whither shall we go up?” Why go up and take the land God promised us? “Our brethren have discouraged our heart.” Those brethren were supposed to be the mightiest men, the leaders sent to spy out the land, and they came back with a weak, scary report: “The people is greater and taller than we; the cities are great and walled up to heaven; and moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakims there.”

Those so-called leaders made the people believe God was setting them up to be destroyed by the Canaanites, instead of being with them to overthrow the Canaanites and take the land that was rightfully ours.

Be mindful who you give ear to; such people are marked for destruction. “And the men, which Moses sent to search the land, who returned, and made all the congregation to murmur against him, by bringing up a slander upon the land, Even those men that did bring up the evil report upon the land, died by the plague before the Lord.”

Do you want to be wrapped up in that foolishness? Guard your heart and your ears with all diligence, and mark the people who speak contrary to what the leaders are teaching you.

sense.text: “Hold fast the form of sound words, which thou hast heard of me”: the words leadership has taught you, “in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus.” Those sound words are also the words you should be studying to show yourself approved unto God.

precepts.why:
“So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” Faith, belief, comes by hearing, and the word of God builds your faith unto salvation.

Bishop Yawasap breaks it down: brothers and sisters come into this truth excited, running and putting their effort into the scriptures. Then they begin to entertain other things, and the commandments and the words of the Most High get less attention. The more you operate outside the aura of God, the more you entertain evil and justify it, maybe the judgment isn’t that bad, and then it happens, and it is too late. There is an effort to pull us away from here; that is what social media and television are about, keeping the mind distracted from what we read here.

Faith cometh by hearing: be in the Bible and be around brothers and sisters who are in the Bible. When you pull away and separate yourself, you are on the way to destruction, as the aura of God gets weaker and the aura of sin greater. You have to be hearing the word of God; it is a conscious thing, a discipline against the push of temptation and of all the things you used to do. If you get weak in what we read here, those other spirits will seduce you, and the next thing you know you are receiving the judgment of sin.

“Above all, taking the shield of faith”, and faith comes by hearing the word of God. What do you do with a shield? You are on guard; you are protecting. “Wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked”: but only if you build up your faith with the word of God. Otherwise the fiery darts of the wicked penetrate and take you out.

So we have to hear the word of God as much as we possibly can, to quench the fiery darts of the wicked and endure to the end: having done all, to stand.

sense.text:
“Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs.” Music is not inherently evil. There is music that comes from the Most High: spiritual songs that teach and admonish you. You feel weak in the gym, a righteous song comes on, one with the king, and you hit a new max. “Singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord”: not drill and evil music.

As Bishop Kani said, music, the melody, programs you: we are all programmed, either with evil or with righteousness. When the little ones get turned up to the righteous music, those instructions are being sealed in their heads. One with the king: that is instruction. The Lord always gives a way to escape, and there is enough righteous music, The Souls of the Saints over and over, that we need not go to the wicked for motivation.

“Despise not the discourse of the wise, but acquaint thyself with their proverbs.” God says do not despise the conversation of the wise. “For of them thou shalt learn instruction, and how to serve great men with ease.”

“Miss not the discourse of the elders”: don’t miss the discourse of our elders, “for they also learned of their fathers, and of them thou shalt learn understanding, and to give answer as need requireth.” That is how the word becomes fitted in your lips. We have to acquaint ourselves with their proverbs: you walk around still quoting wicked lyrics, racky blicky, when you are supposed to be quoting the Bishops’ sound bites. That is supposed to be second nature to you.

precepts.why:
“Let thy talk be with the wise, and all thy communication in the law of the most High.” Your communication has to be in accordance with the laws of God. Period. That is what the Bible says.

“And let just men eat and drink with thee”: just men, not whisperers and backbiters, “and let thy glorying be in the fear of the Lord.” That is righteous conversation.

sense.text:
“He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, that shaketh his hands from holding of bribes, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil.” The Lord gives the criteria of different forms of discipline. He stops his ears against murderous plots: you may say you don’t talk with anybody about sliding and murdering, but you may be listening to it.

It is not only blood but all participation in evil, and that includes welcoming its counsel. How do you welcome somebody? You let them in the door, through the gate. Refusing to hear schemes of bloodshed rejects any part in violence. Some things you cannot help, like the music in the store, and you tune it out; but nobody should be willfully welcoming evil into their spirit. Christ calls his disciples away from hatred toward the peace that marks the children of God, so you should not be listening to anything hateful.

And he shuts his eyes against evil: holiness requires deliberate refusal to entertain what God condemns, visual or audio. The righteous do not let evil shape the heart, and that is what it does: let it into your spirit and it reshapes your brain, neuroplasticity, the cords of sin, the evil pathways that destroy your mind. Such conduct does not earn salvation, but it marks those who fear the Lord and look to him for refuge. You discipline your ears; you guard your ear gate.

“He shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks: bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure.” He or she that guards the gates shall dwell on high: that is who is going to get the kingdom. So strengthen yourselves to guard the ear gate with all diligence.
